profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary:
I am an Android developer who love programming by heart. I love to solve challenging problems, and I understand an optimal solution is not solely based on how short the code can be. Instead a good solution is a compromise of timeline, resources, feasibility, maintainability and many other factors.

I enjoy exploring new technology and libraries. Rather than blindly adopting those shiny new things, I would always try to understand the motivation and the problems those new tools try to resolve before I start using them. I have helped my team adopted many patterns and tools, including rxjava, dagger, Kotlin, and Android architecture components.

I like to make friends even at work. I know I can always learn something from others, and I enjoy sharing my knowledge back to them as well. I have done more than five internal presentations, given two talks in Kotlin DFW meetup, and written blogposts about Android and Kotlin. Topics include java time, markdown, reactive programming, functional programming with guava, and custom views.

I also spend extra hours on improving development tools. I have built custom gradle plugins, configured Jenkins plugins and jobs, utilized docker for CI and testings. Development should be straightforward and enjoyable, and developers should spend time on coding, not waiting.

While I don't work for money and sponsorship, I can't commit to a long-term relationship without those. If you or your company are not ready for a long-term relationship, please let's save both of us some time for finding the Mr. Right.

Skills: java; andorid; cast; kotlin; spring boot; micro services; git; restful api; linux; markdown; oop; groovy; gradle; jenkins; ci; json; apiary; docker;

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.locationName: Mountain View, California, United States · Hybrid

positions.title: Senior Android Software Engineer I
positions.description:
The platform codebase is built upon different software components. They are designed and implemented by interfaces and configured at each client app via dependency injections. Instead of hardcoded feature flags, functionalities and configurations can be altered at either compile time or run time to meet various requirements.

We constantly review and update our tech stacks to make sure our platform is performant, maintainable, and enjoyable. We have incorporated Guava, RxJava, Kotlin, and Architecture components for a while.

The components include:
* video players,
* ad components,
* caption sources,
* chromecast,
* authentication / authorization,
* and many others.

positions.title: Research Assistant for Java Web Application
positions.description:
Developed an online interactive teaching platform using natural language processing in Java.
The system allowed approximately 1,500 online teachers and students login and discuss topics in class using computers or mobile devices rather than papers.
